title: Plurality Is Stablest for Small Positive Correlations: A Gaussian Simplex Theorem
summary: For each fixed number of cells, proves a dimension-independent qualitative interval of small positive correlations on which the balanced regular-simplex partition maximizes Gaussian noise stability, with equality rigidity.
verification: Analytic all-cell proof, including the attributed first-moment covariance argument, with published geometric inputs. Warning-free LaTeX build and all-page visual inspection; the current PDF-only review and archive reproduction are recorded in verification.json. No external specialist review or formal verification.

abstract:
For every fixed $k\ge2$, we prove that the central regular-simplex
partition maximizes Gaussian noise stability among all equal-measure
measurable $k$-cell partitions in every dimension $d\ge k-1$, for all
sufficiently small positive correlations. The interval is independent of $d$, and
equality determines the simplex partition up to orthogonal maps, labels
and cylindrical extension. The proof combines Zhang's first-moment
comparison with compactness for measurable label changes, normalized by
their exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck score loss. Weighted Gaussian tightness
gives a limiting facet flux whose sharp quadratic cost forces
rotationality; moment alignment removes that mode. The threshold is
qualitative and may depend on the number of cells.
